title: Capture Every Sales Call into Your Go-to-Market Repo
summary: Cargo's call-capture cookbook collects your recorded calls every morning, writes one log entry per call into your go-to-market repository, and promotes a claim into context only once two calls back it, as one pull request a human reviews.
body_markdown:
**To capture every sales call into your go-to-market repo, deploy Cargo’s call-capture cookbook: one Claude Code agent that, every morning at 07:00 UTC, collects your recorded calls, writes one log entry per call, and promotes a claim into` context/` only once two independent calls back it.** It all lands as one pull request a human reviews. The agent never merges it, emails anyone or writes to a CRM.


What the cookbook deploys, from its code in[getcargohq/gtm-skills](https://github.com/getcargohq/gtm-skills/tree/main/call-capture) on 2026-10-16: 4 resources (one agent, two connectors, one folder) plus a collector script with 9 call recorder adapters, one daily cron, and a cap of 12 calls written up per run.


## The problem, and the answer#


What a team learns on calls usually stays in a recording nobody reopens, so the same objection gets relearned every quarter. The answer is to treat calls as a sensor: a fixed script pulls the transcripts, an agent writes them up as markdown in the repository every other agent already reads, and a claim only becomes company knowledge when it repeats.


## How it works, end to end#


1. **The cron fires** at 07:00 UTC (` 0 7 * * *` ), after the recorder has finished processing yesterday’s calls.
2. **The agent clones your repository.** It is a Claude Code harness agent, so its working tree is the go-to-market repo itself. Which repository it clones is resolved from your checkout’s git origin at deploy.
3. **It runs the collector** ,` scripts/call-capture/collect/calls.ts` . The script pulls every call in a three-day rolling window whose transcript is ready, drops calls with only internal attendees, and writes one raw file per call into` cadence/log/raw/calls/` . No language model is involved in this step, and the agent is told not to fetch calls itself or edit the script.
4. **It writes up each pending call** as` cadence/log/calls/<date>-<account>.md` : what was said, then Objections, Competitors mentioned, Buying or expansion signals and Product asks, then the actions as checkboxes. A call is pending when its recorder id appears in no entry yet, so one call gets one entry, ever.
5. **It caps the run at 12 calls** : every pending call from the last 30 days first, newest first, then the oldest pending calls, so a backlog drains without delaying this week’s follow-ups. An action older than 30 days is prefixed` STALE-CHECK` , because a backfilled commitment is a question, not a task.
6. **It promotes what repeats.** A claim reaches` context/` only on its second independent occurrence (two accounts, or one account on two calls), and the context file cites both log entries.
7. **It opens one pull request** , titled` \[call-capture\] scribe <date>` , whose body states four numbers: calls captured, written up fresh, written up from the backlog, and still pending. If nothing was captured and nothing was pending, it opens nothing.


After a human merges, the next` cargo-ai project deploy` syncs` context/` into the workspace, where your other agents read it.


## The recorders it reads#


Nine recorder adapters ship, and you pick one with a typed constant,` RECORDER` in` scripts/call-capture/collect/config.ts` . A name that is not one of the nine fails the typecheck.


Recorder Adapter status


Avoma Verified against a live workspace


Clari Copilot Written from the vendor’s API docs

The eight unverified adapters say so on every run. Check yours before deploying: running the collector script with` --recorder=<slug> --dry-run` lists the calls it would capture and writes nothing. A recorder that does not ship is one new adapter file plus one entry in the registry.


## What it needs and what it costs#


- **A go-to-market repository** with` context/` and` cadence/` at its root, the shape` cargo-ai project init` scaffolds.
- **A GitHub connector** , the agent’s only write path: clone, branch, push, pull request.
- **An Anthropic connector** , the model the agent runs on.
- **Your recorder’s API key** as a workspace environment variable, not a file:` cargo-ai workspaceManagement envVar create --key CALL_RECORDER_API_KEY --secret` . With no` --value` , the CLI reads it from the environment variable of the same name.
- **Your email domain** in` INTERNAL_DOMAIN` , or every internal standup is captured as a customer call.
- ` @cargo-ai/cli` 1.0.89 or later and` @cargo-ai/cdk` 1.0.67 or later.


The cookbook calls no connector action, so it spends no per-record credits. The recurring cost is the daily agent run, billed as language model tokens through your Anthropic connector, and the 12-call cap is the cost control as much as the review control. The collector talks to your recorder directly, so your recorder plan’s API limits apply.


## What it will not do#


- Contact a customer, send email or Slack messages, or write to a CRM.
- Merge its own pull request or push to the default branch.
- Edit or delete a raw capture or an existing log entry.
- Touch` plan/` or` infra/` .
- Write a one-off claim into` context/` .
- Summarize one call right now. That is a read against your recorder’s own API and needs nothing deployed.


The cookbook is marked to-be-approved: its acceptance test has not yet been run end to end against a live workspace, so review` cargo-ai project plan` before you deploy.


## Deploy it#


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com
cargo-ai   project   add   cookbook/call-capture
cargo-ai   project   plan
cargo-ai   project   deploy


```


Signing up from the CLI needs no browser and no card, and comes with 100 free credits. Run` project add` inside your go-to-market project; with no project yet,` cargo-ai project init <dir> --cookbook call-capture` scaffolds one with the cookbook in it. The[call-capture cookbook page](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/call-capture) has the full file list and the placeholders to edit before deploying.


Once calls land in the log,[track the next steps promised on them](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/track-next-steps-promised-on-sales-calls) , and[prep the next meeting from the calendar](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/prep-every-external-meeting-from-the-calendar) with what the last one said.


## Frequently asked questions#


Nine adapters ship: Avoma, Clari Copilot, Fathom, Fireflies.ai, Gong, Grain, Granola, Modjo and tl;dv. Avoma is verified against a live workspace; the other eight were written from each vendor’s API docs, and` --dry-run` checks one against your account before you deploy.


No. It calls no connector action. The cost is one agent run a day, billed as language model tokens through your Anthropic connector, and the cap of 12 calls per run bounds it.


Every other agent reads` context/` before it acts, so a claim written there from one offhand remark becomes something the whole company believes. One occurrence stays in the call’s log entry; the second promotes it, citing both calls.


No. Its only write path is the GitHub connector, it opens one pull request a day, and a human merges it.
